title: Forest-floor plants did not show a consistent recovery signal related to nitrogen deposition in Swedish (1994-2024) and French (2005-2022) forest inventory plots
abstract: We tested if forest-floor plant communities shifted toward nitrogen-demanding species where atmospheric N deposition was high, and if this shift reversed after deposition decreased. We used two systematic national forest inventories: Swedish NFI presence-absence data (40,497 tract-years, 1994-2024, permanent tracts revisited at about 10-year intervals) and French IGN IFN releves (106,869 plots, 2005-2022). Exposure was EMEP MSC-W rv5.6 total N deposition (0.1 degree). Species N niches were EIVE 1.0 values. Temperature came from E-OBS. The pre-specified outcome was the community mean EIVE-N of the field layer. In Sweden, with site and latitude-band x year fixed effects, 1990-94 deposition did not predict its change: -0.017 +- 0.027 (1994-2008) and -0.010 +- 0.014 (2008-2024) units per decade per 5 kg N/ha/yr. A rise and then a fall of the mean occurred in all deposition terciles. In France, the mean decreased more where 2001-05 deposition was high (-0.053 +- 0.015, mainly after 2013). But this value decreased to -0.028 +- 0.019 with geographic trend controls and came only from north of 47 N. A secondary species-trait composite with cell-clustered errors showed that N-demanding species gained at high-deposition Swedish tracts in 1994-2008 (z = 2.6, only in the south) and decreased in France in 2013-2022 (z = -2.8), but only in southern France. Thus neither country gave a consistent signal of deposition-related recovery across metrics and regions. We also report a pitfall: when the exposure grid is finer than the location fixed effects, an omitted exposure main effect produced a false rise-then-fall pattern (z = +3.9/-4.8). Limitations: modelled deposition, no stand-age data, mosses and lichens not tested, and the composite test was added after the primary result.
